question.text: In a UNIFIED fund structure, commitments from both domestic and offshore investors are:

answer.text: Pooled into two separate vehicles — one onshore and one offshore — which invest independently
Pooled into a single domestic (onshore) AIF registered in India, with offshore investors investing via FPI/FDI route
Collected by the manager and placed in personal brokerage accounts
Split by nationality with offshore investors bypassing SEBI registration entirely

explanation.text: The Logic: In a Unified Structure, commitments from both domestic and foreign investors are pooled into ONE domestic (onshore) AIF. Offshore investors route through FPI/FDI automatic route into the same AIF. The India-based manager earns fees at the onshore level. One pooling vehicle, mixed investor base. The Trap: Option A describes a Parallel Structure (two vehicles). Option C is fabricated. Option D is wrong — SEBI/FEMA compliance is still required. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D/A/B all touch this taxonomy. XIX-E goes deeper given Cat III's complex onshore/offshore routing options. Manager's Pro-Tip: Unified is the cleanest structure commercially — one NAV, one fee pool, one strike. But verify the offshore investors' home-country tax treatment via DTAA before closing them, or the tax drag kills the simplicity.
